subject: Microbiology
subtopic: Plague: organism, flea transmission, bubonic/pneumonic/septicemic disease, diagnosis, treatment and prevention
concept: Plague is a potentially life-threatening zoonotic infection caused by Yersinia pestis, usually transmitted by infected rodent fleas or contact with infected animals.

content.definition: Plague is a potentially life-threatening zoonotic infection caused by Yersinia pestis, usually transmitted by infected rodent fleas or contact with infected animals.
content.explanation: Y. pestis is a Gram-negative coccobacillus with important antiphagocytic virulence factors. After flea inoculation it can multiply in regional lymphatic tissue, producing buboes; hematogenous spread causes septicemic disease and pulmonary involvement can produce pneumonic plague.
content.mechanism: Y. pestis is a Gram-negative coccobacillus with important antiphagocytic virulence factors. After flea inoculation it can multiply in regional lymphatic tissue, producing buboes; hematogenous spread causes septicemic disease and pulmonary involvement can produce pneumonic plague.
content.structure: Clinically important organism-specific structural and biologic features are summarized in the explanation and terminology fields.
content.function: The pathogen's biologic properties determine transmission, tissue tropism, clinical manifestations and diagnostic strategy.
causes: Respiratory droplets from pneumonic plague in close contact
effects: Bubonic plague: fever and painful regional lymphadenopathy (bubo)
Septicemic plague: systemic toxicity and bacteremia
Pneumonic plague: severe pneumonia and respiratory transmission
content.clinical_relevance: This is an official Hematology microbiology syllabus organism/disease. Yersinia pestis and Plague should be interpreted using current diagnostic and treatment guidance.
content.diagnosis: Diagnosis may involve culture, molecular testing or other laboratory methods on appropriate specimens such as bubo aspirate, blood or respiratory samples; notify the laboratory because of biosafety concerns.
content.treatment: Plague is treatable with prompt antibiotics. Therapy should be started urgently when clinical suspicion is high rather than waiting for definitive laboratory confirmation; public-health contact management is important for pneumonic exposure.
